realtime-bot: [ALERT] realtime-p95-regression detected for route /v1/generate-stream in eu-central-1 · p95 baseline 310ms -> 1.4s · p99 920ms -> 5.2s · rolling 2m · severity: high · pagerduty: oncall
pagerduty-bot: Incident routed to kevin (oncall) · please acknowledge: https://pagerduty.example/INC-99921
kevin: ack. i'm on. first quick checks: dashboards, recent deploys, infra events. anyone seeing deploys in last 6h?ashwin: no app deploys for streaming route in last 6h. noticing a big traffic spike (~3.2x) starting 11:42 UTC, likely a marketing push hitting EU region. might be contributing.
maria: dashboard snapshot -> https://dash.redwood/streams/eu-central shows dispatch.queue_time p95 1.2s, dispatch.queue_time p99 4.9s, stream_chunk_timeout rate up 18x. Also KV-cache hit rate dropped from 86% -> 42% around 11:44
lee: infra alerts: autoscaler started 4 scaleups at 11:45, several pods in dedicated-pool-eu reported rapid OOMKill for model-worker at 11:46 then one node had `nvidia-smi` driver restart message. looks like a transient GPU driver reset on node `wn-eu-07`
kevin: that lines up. so: traffic surge + gpu resets -> cache cold -> queueing -> streaming stalls. immediate mitigation options: 1) throttle* or shed non-critical streaming sessions, 2) shift a percentage of streaming traffic to fallback-pool-eu, 3) temporarily disable streaming (degrade to non-streaming sync) for high-latency clients. prefer minimal-customer-impact path: partial traffic shift + enable streaming_prefetch
maria: agree. can we shift 25% of eu streaming to fallback-pool-eu (older stable nodes) and enable `streaming_prefetch=true` for that route so the fallback uses warmed cache? also cordon `wn-eu-07` and remove from rotation
kevin: running rdctl commands now:
```
rdctl routing set --route /v1/generate-stream --percent 25 --to-pool fallback-pool-eu --policy gradual
rdctl pool update fallback-pool-eu --set streaming_prefetch=true
kubectl cordon wn-eu-07 && kubectl drain wn-eu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
kevin: routing change applied (gradual 25%) · prefetch enabled on fallback-pool-eu · cordon/drain initiated on wn-eu-07
support-bot: Notification sent to customers impacted in EU region (subset) · reference: incident INC-99921
ashwin: observing metrics: p95 dropping to ~720ms within 3m for EU region, p99 trending down from 5.2s to 2.1s. stream_chunk_timeout rate reduced by ~60% on shifted traffic
lee: infra note: node wn-eu-07 driver logs show nvlink recovery + subsequent worker restart. created ticket INF-9999 for hw/driver deep-dive and flagged warranty check for GPU unit
kevin: follow-ups while monitoring: 1) keep 25% shift for 20m, 2) if stable, incrementally move back 10% at a time, 3) add alert for `dispatch.queue_time > 1s` on streaming routes, 4) add alert for `kvcache.hit_rate < 60%` per-pool
maria: adding runbook changes: will include auto-shift policy when node reset events >1 within 10m or kvcache drop >30% during traffic spikes. Also add guidance to prefer `gradual` routing to avoid double-coldstarts
kevin: note on root cause hypothesis: combination of sudden traffic spike and a single GPU driver reset caused cascading worker restart and cache coldstart. Contributing: autoscaler reaction time, no immediate pool-quarantine automation, no alert for rapid kvcache drop
ashwin: customer impact summary for postmortem: ~2.9% of EU streaming sessions experienced stalls/timeouts; error rate for stream endpoints rose from 0.03% -> 1.1% during spike window. No data corruption reported. Outreach: support already contacted affected accounts and posted status on status.redwood.ai
kevin: paging cleared for oncall. handing monitoring to maria for 30m watch. created infra ticket INF-9999 and ops ticket OPS-4721 for runbook changes
maria: will monitor and post final resolution when p99 <900ms and error rate <0.2% for 30 consecutive minutes. prepping post-incident summary
lee: added node `wn-eu-07` to quarantine label in pool to prevent autoscaler reusing it until HW checks pass
ashwin: thanks team. open action items: 1) INF-9999 hardware triage, 2) OPS-4721 runbook + alerts, 3) add canary step in deploy pipeline to detect q-compact/driver combos under load, 4) review autoscaler sensitivity for bursty traffic
maria: update at 12:15 UTC: p99 now 610ms, p95 250ms, stream timeouts back to baseline. moving to postmortem and closing incident in 30m if stable. :white_check_mark:
